text:
Bore Da/Good morning

I can confirm that we hold no records regarding the Williams family or the deed of land transfer associated with Daniel Thomas and the Bute Estate. This involved a detailed pc records enquiry of our heritage catalogue, a physical search on the Biographical records we hold, and a query of all records we have regarding transfers of material.

With regard to Great House Farm (Ty Mawr) all I could find was an extract in the South Wales Spectator October 1974 (page 58) which was one page written by A.L.Ducie on his visit to the property.

The copy of the conveyance or land transfer associated with Daniel Thomas and the Bute Estate If we could get some more information relating to this item which will include the title of the item and author. If possible



You are more than welcome to attend Cathays library to view the page.

If you are unable we can send the page digitally to you; however this will incur fees.

Please see below a cost breakdown and a list of information requested (we ask for this so that we can send you an invoice). Once this has been completed we will aim to complete your query as soon as possible.

David,

Bore Da / Good Morning,

Will do. And thanks for your prompt reply.

Please also clarify whether any searches were undertaken beyond deeds and title documents, as my enquiry extends to a wider range of historical materials relating to Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough.

Family records and longstanding local accounts indicate that a copy of the conveyance or land transfer associated with Daniel Thomas and the Bute Estate may at one time have been available through Cardiff's library or local studies collections. The Williams family relied upon documentary evidence relating to the farm during disputes concerning occupation and ownership during the twentieth century, and family members consistently referred to such records.

I therefore respectfully request that Cathays Branch and Heritage Library, or the appropriate Cardiff Council department, undertake or arrange a search of any relevant holdings, including:

• Local studies collections and vertical files. • Heritage and local history indexes. • Newspaper cuttings collections. • Photographic collections. • Map collections. • Catalogue entries and accession records. • References to Great House Farm, Ty Mawr, Llandough. • References to Daniel Thomas, the Bute Estate, quarry agreements, land exchanges, or conveyances. • References to John Williams, Mary Williams, or other members of the Williams family associated with the farm. • Records indicating whether any such material was transferred to Glamorgan Archives or another repository.

In particular, if any relevant material was formerly held by Cardiff Libraries or Cardiff Council but subsequently transferred, withdrawn, re-catalogued, or otherwise relocated, I would be grateful for any information identifying where those records are now held and any catalogue references that may assist my research.

If this request would be more appropriately handled under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 or Environmental Information Regulations 2004, please treat it accordingly or transfer it internally to the relevant department.

The purpose of my enquiry is to identify surviving historical records relating to Great House Farm and the Williams family's connection to the property. Any guidance, references, finding aids, catalogue entries, or archive references would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to hearing from you.

Diolch yn fawr, Regards,

Sion Buckler Esq. (Ret'd Sgt)
Williams/ Buckler Family Researcher and Representative | https://bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz
